name: Landsat 9
keyLesson: Sun-synchronous orbits guarantee identical sun angle and shadows for every repeat pass, making long-term environmental change detection accurate.

name: Kepler Space Telescope
keyLesson: Exoplanet transit detection requires extreme pointing stability (reaction wheels) and thermal control so instrument noise doesn't drown out tiny starlight dips.

name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO)
keyLesson: Low lunar orbits face intense gravitational anomalies (mascons) and communication occultation during far-side passes, requiring autonomous onboard scheduling.

name: PACE (Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, ocean Ecosystem)
keyLesson: Hyperspectral imaging produces immense raw data rates, requiring high-bandwidth Ka-band downlinks and prioritized onboard data compression.

name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO)
keyLesson: At 1.52 AU, solar flux drops to 43% of Earth nominal; twin 20 m² sun-tracking solar wings paired with a 3.0 m Ka/X-band parabolic dish enable gigabit Martian science return via the DSN.

name: Magellan Venus Radar Mapper
orbit: Venus Polar Elliptical / Cloud-Top Orbit (~300 km, 85.5°)
keyLesson: Opaque sulfuric acid clouds block visible light at Venus, making Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) essential, while 191% solar flux demands active thermal management.

name: Europa Clipper
orbit: Jovian / Europa Science Orbit (200 km belts)
keyLesson: Inside Jupiter's fierce synchrotron radiation belts at 5.2 AU (3.7% sunlight), a titanium-aluminum radiation vault, rad-hard flight computers, and massive 102 m² solar wings keep electronics alive.

name: Cassini–Huygens Saturn/Titan Orbiter
orbit: Titan Flyby & Hydrocarbon Sea Mapping Orbit (1,200 km)
keyLesson: At 9.5 AU around Saturn and Titan, sunlight is just 1.1% of Earth's—rendering solar panels unviable and making Plutonium-238 Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators (RTGs) mandatory.

name: Psyche Asteroid Orbiter
orbit: 16 Psyche Metallic Asteroid Polar Orbit (120 km)
keyLesson: Surveying the exposed metal protoplanet core 16 Psyche pairs Magnetometer Booms and Neutron Spectroscopy with NASA's groundbreaking Deep Space Optical Communications (DSOC) laser link.

name: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)
primaryInstruments: NIRCam / NIRSpec / MIRI (6.5m Cryogenic Optical-IR Telescope)
keyLesson: Positioned at Sun-Earth L2 to eliminate Earth eclipses and infrared glare, JWST achieves milliarcsecond pointing stability and cryogenic optics via precision star trackers and active thermal isolation.
